The Seal of Biliteracy is an award given by the Vermont Organization of Classics and Language Educators under the authorization of the Agency of Education in recognition of students who have studied and attained proficiency in two or more languages [including English] by high school graduation. The Seal of Biliteracy takes the form of a seal that appears on the transcript or diploma of the graduating senior and is a statement of accomplishment for future employers and for college admissions. More information will be provided by World Language teachers.
courses.notes: One heading covering Spanish 5 / AP / Seal of Biliteracy; seniors eligible for the Seal of Biliteracy.

courses.description: This one-semester class provides a foundation for 9th graders to do self-exploration about who they are as individuals. Emphasis is placed on discovering their interests, skills, and strengths and connecting them to personal, educational, and professional goals and/or pathways. Students will learn how to communicate professionally by creating a résumé, participate in a mock interview, and write a professional thank you letter; research careers of interest and connect their personal interests to career fields; and begin to plan a roadmap through high school that allows them to pursue flexible pathways and classes that are connected to their interests.

Building off students’ previous experience in DSH middle school courses, this class will utilize food and “systems thinking” as a means to understanding the three primary aspects of sustainability: social equity, economic fairness, and environmental health. In this project-based course, students will spend much of the semester developing culinary and marketing skills through food production and distribution connected to Harwood’s “Harvest of the Month” programming and other school-wide events. Students will also participate in group activities and field trips that examine the impact of social and environmental systems on the individual, their immediate community, and the larger world. Finally, this course will utilize guest speakers to provide students with first-hand perspectives on potential career tracks related to the culinary, service, agricultural, health, and public policy industries.

Is there something you wish you could do, learn, experience, or make at school? In Idea Lab, students will be supported to design, experience, and make their own projects. This could look like designing and prototyping a product, learning a new skill or craft (or leveling up an existing one), taking a deep dive into researching a topic of interest, or pursuing a project related to a club or extracurricular activity. Students will explore interests, ask questions, research their topic, connect with community experts, manage time, document their progress, set goals, prioritize their work, and most importantly spend time developing their project artifact. Class takes place in the Exploratory Lab where students will have access to a variety of high and low tech tools and materials.This class will not only let you learn what you want, but will teach you the career and college ready skills you need to organize and manage long term projects.
courses.notes: Duration: Semester, can be taken multiple times

courses.description: Documenting the World, a course supporting the amazing travel opportunities offered at Harwood, will provide students with a project-based opportunity to deeply explore the immensely complex concept of CULTURE: How is it created? How do we consume it? How does it impact ourselves and the way we view the world? In this semester course open to ALL grade levels, students will first spend time digging into their own experiences to examine these broad questions through community interviews and the development of multimedia-based stories. As the class progresses, the focus shifts to the discipline of cultural anthropology and the skills of ethnographic inquiry; students will be introduced to the rich cultures of each destination visited by Harwood’s travel study program - Denmark, Columbia, Rwanda, and India. Ultimately, this course is designed to provide participants with a window into the world of others and reinforce the idea that culture is much more than a set of unique values and behaviors that divide us from one another. The more we explore diverse cultures, the more we realize just how similar our lived experiences are.

Work Experience provides students the opportunity to explore their interests in specific career areas through short-term paid work experiences, while at the same time, addressing learning expectations. Students must submit a training agreement, learning goals, employer evaluations and student reflections to complete the course.
courses.notes: program; Duration: Semester and Year-long

courses.description: Internship provides a unique opportunity for students to experience career areas of interest. This is typically a semester or year long commitment. Students work with Next Step staff to explore their areas of interest to develop prospective internship placements. Students are supported in writing a resume, preparing for an interview and developing their learning goals. Once a placement is developed, the student works with the Internship Coordinator and the site mentor to align learning objectives to the proficiencies and performance indicators. In addition, if appropriate, a content-area teacher will serve as the academic advisor, assessing students' final projects and learning. ●​ Students will track the amount of hours spent doing internship related tasks ●​ Students will write a weekly reflection based on their learning goals, self-direction and other learning proficiencies, if appropriate ●​ Students will demonstrate employability skills while at their internship site ●​ Students will complete projects/products to demonstrate their attainment of the performance indicators ●​ Students are expected to meet all deadlines
courses.notes: program; description says typically a semester or year long commitment.

courses.description: Independent Study provides an opportunity for students to explore a topic of interest. It is available for students who are unable to schedule an existing class or to create a course offering that is unique based on student interest. Students can receive support in creating a proposal for consideration through Connected Learning. A teacher in the designated content area is required to review authentic assessments aligned with the performance indicators that are addressed in the study.
courses.notes: program; Duration: Semester and Year-long

courses.description: Career and Personal Planning (CPP) is designed to reinforce and refine the habits-of-being necessary for success in the world beyond high school. In CPP, students will be given space to explore potential ways to take that “next step” after graduation and set post-secondary goals that are personally significant to their educational and/or career aspirations. Because the class has been developed in conjunction with Community College of Vermont’s “Intro to College & Career” course, CPP students will also officially enroll at CCV, utilize the college’s digital learning platform, and earn a non-degree-bearing credit for successfully completing the course; however, it will NOT count towards a student’s 2 dual-enrollment opportunities. CPP will focus on concrete outcomes: students will walk away from the course with a plan for your immediate future and the ability to navigate the complexities of a rapidly-changing society.
courses.notes: Developed with Community College of Vermont "Intro to College & Career"; earns a non-degree-bearing CCV credit that does NOT count toward the 2 dual-enrollment opportunities.

courses.description: Interested in working with your classmates as entrepreneurs to run a business? Through hands-on activities, student-led business opportunities and a culminating pitch project, students will gain real-world experience turning ideas into viable business ventures that turn a profit. In Adventure in Business you will: ●​ Use creative and critical thinking skills to imagine a product or service that meets a community need. ●​ Develop a business plan using collective skills and available resources. ●​ Participate in management positions of interest such as marketing, product development, sales, advertising or communications. ●​ Launch, operate and evaluate the success of your student run business and/or personal business plan. ●​ Collaborate with small business owners, entrepreneurial experts and the Vermont Small Business Development Center. ●​ Practice presentation skills culminating in a formal business plan pitch. ●​ Explore future career interests and opportunities in entrepreneurship and small business.

The Harwood Community Learning Center is a personalized, community-based program open to all juniors and seniors at Harwood. Students enrolled in this daily, double-block experience receive English, history, science, math and elective (career exploration) credits. HCLC attempts to approach education holistically. Classes balance experiential and traditional learning models while also providing both individualized and group-oriented academic instruction. The program is built around long-term, interest-based projects. As students move through the interdisciplinary project structure, they conduct research, access community experts, and gather resources best suited to the development of a final product that showcases new learning in an authentic way. At its core, HCLC provides students with the following: 1.​ A small, tight-knit learning community where students are approached as individuals 2.​ A flexible educational environment that incorporates student interest into core academics and provides ample one-on-one support 3.​ A focus on future planning to help students get organized for their life after high school
